claims: Tree navigation retains branches in one file while fork/clone create separate sessions; compaction retains original entries.

title: JSONL tree projection, model entries and file creation
claims: SessionManager exposes create/open/continueRecent/inMemory/forkFrom and same-file branch operations.
Initial file creation waits for a user or assistant message; model-change entries store provider/model ID without a full endpoint or egress contract.
Synchronous JSONL writes do not create an atomic transaction with Splyce receipts.

title: Model mutation and tree-navigation guards
claims: setModel checks auth, changes model state, appends model_change, optionally persists defaults and emits model_select.
Inspected setModel/cycleModel mutation paths have no streaming guard; navigateTree explicitly rejects streaming or concurrent compaction/navigation.
abort waits for idle; Splyce still needs admission and model-contract fencing.

title: Session replacement ownership, cancellation and outgoing-turn settlement
claims: newSession/switchSession/fork belong to AgentSessionRuntime and emit cancellable before-switch/fork hooks.
Teardown aborts and settles outgoing work before shutdown/disposal; replacement then constructs and rebinds fresh runtime state.
Fork validates entry/position and can reject unsaved persisted sources; failed construction is not proven atomic rollback.

title: RPC and print/JSON dispatch differences
claims: RPC set_model resolves an available pair then calls the unguarded AgentSession setter; input handlers can overlap.
Print/JSON bind replacement actions to AgentSessionRuntime; print text maps error/aborted/truncated terminal responses to failure.
RPC supplies extension UI messaging while the extension runner defaults to false/undefined prompts without UI.
